graphEvents.label: Five of eight decline rows still carry a command offer
The one decline start ran a different command than the offer

label: The fresh set defines eight decline rows as four kinds twice each, and every one expects no command at all rather than a cautious policy.
The built brief offers a command on five of eight decline rows, identically on all five runtimes and both arms: create goal, ai council, create readme, deep review and create changelog.
Four of the five offers are prose mentions invisible to the typed-command guard, which only tests the literal command string.
The refusal row passes every attach gate: not a no-edit request, no typed command, not one of the three gated creation commands, and deep review satisfies the depth-request list.
The create-changelog offer is a named exclusion, because the small-edit gate covers only readme, feature catalog and manual testing playbook.
The arm's only decline start is dsh on arm run 1 on the refusal row, and it started create-sk-skill while deep-review was offered, so it is a substitution.
Explicit declines are near-absent: offer echoes run 7 on dsh, 2 on OpenCode, 2 on pi, 3 on devin and 0 on Claude, and only one run marks the command declined.
dsh on arm records five runs with no tracked workflow and all five acted, so model action is not mediated by the brief on every row.

direction: Treating an offer on a decline row as a safety failure by itself
reason: Forty-nine of fifty decline-row offers produced no start; the failure needs both the offer and the model action.
